close_reason: Fixed in de2b2df. Added #[non_exhaustive] to SlowModeError plus SlowModeError::new(retry_after) constructor. External consumers MUST use the constructor; field-init is forbidden outside the defining crate. The TrackingBackend in tests/common/mod.rs (separate crate root for each test binary) migrated to the constructor; the rustdoc reference to the old shape was also updated. Pre-1.0 / pre-publish; additive #[non_exhaustive] is free.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:222-226

  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  pub struct SlowModeError {
      pub retry_after: jmap_types::UTCDate,
  }

SlowModeError is part of the public ChatBackend trait surface
(returned by Err of slow_mode_check). Consumers implementing
production rate-limiters construct this type, so it is in their
build-time surface.

The struct has one public field and is NOT #[non_exhaustive].
Adding any field later — a retry hint string, a sender-facing
error code, a backoff multiplier, a "this is your N-th throttle
in M minutes" counter — is a major-version-breaking change.

Compare with ChatLimits (backend.rs:89-110) and EmojiSetOp
(backend.rs:194-204), both correctly #[non_exhaustive]. The
omission here is asymmetric, not principled.

Workaround for consumers: none — they have to construct the type
positionally.

Fix:
  #[non_exhaustive]
  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  pub struct SlowModeError {
      pub retry_after: jmap_types::UTCDate,
  }

Plus a `pub fn new(retry_after: UTCDate) -> Self` constructor and
(optionally) a `with_*` builder if more fields land later. Same
pattern as ChatLimits::new + with_max_*.
title: API contract: SlowModeError missing #[non_exhaustive]
